ce_bugs.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Guests are persisted to the DB before the calendar sync call, with no transaction or rollback, so a calendar-sync failure leaves attendees committed without a confirmed invite.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — The CalendarEvent passed to sendAddGuestsEmails never sets the team field, so team members are silently never notified of the added guest.

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — Organizer email subject uses calEvent.attendees[0].name instead of organizer/team name, and new guests are created with an empty name, risking a blank subject.
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:46 — The "Remove email" tooltip text is hardcoded in English instead of using the component's useLocale/t() translation function.

mrv_findings.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` calls a method not defined anywhere in this diff or repo; likely a fabricated API surface that fails to compile or throws at runtime (confidence=60, P0).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:1-174 — only "add guest" is implemented; no remove-guest, edit-guest, or guest-history capability despite the "guest management" framing (confidence=85, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-174 + apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:553-554 — no booking.status/startTime check, so guests can be added to past/cancelled/rejected bookings, triggering confusing calendar syncs and emails for dead events (confidence=75, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-138 — recurring bookings not handled: only the single row matched by bookingId is updated, so a guest added to one occurrence doesn't propagate to sibling occurrences (confidence=65, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — seats-based bookings: attendees inserted via plain createMany with no BookingSeat records and no check against eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, bypassing seat-capacity enforcement (confidence=55, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires BOTH admin AND owner (should likely be OR), excluding legitimate non-owner team admins from managing guests (confidence=70, P1).

Full diff — no automated tests added anywhere for addGuests.schema.ts/handler.ts, AddGuestsDialog.tsx, or MultiEmail.tsx; no test covers permission checks, dedup, or email fan-out (confidence=95, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-81 — uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees/blacklist, never against duplicates within the incoming array itself; schema has no uniqueness refine, so a bypassed-client payload can create duplicate attendee rows (confidence=70, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email send failures are swallowed by `console.log`; mutation still returns success, so notification completeness can't be verified or surfaced (confidence=80, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` collapses to "role===OWNER only", contradicting the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` which implies OR semantics (confidence=75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — EventManager/getUsersCredentials built from the calling session user, not the booking organizer, so a non-organizer attendee invoking this mutation builds calendar context keyed to the wrong (or absent) calendar credentials (confidence=70, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw pre-filter `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`; email-manager's `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check then sends a full re-invite email to attendees who were actually filtered out as duplicates (confidence=80, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-77 — blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming `guest` is compared unnormalized (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), and the existing-attendee dedup (`guest === attendee.email`) has no case normalization either, letting differently-cased duplicates through (confidence=75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-106 — TOCTOU: booking.attendees read once via findFirst then appended via a separate non-transactional update with no optimistic lock or unique constraint, so two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both pass the dedup check and both insert (confidence=70, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` never logs `err`, gives no signal to the caller, and the mutation still reports success even if every email failed (confidence=90, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — blacklist bypass via casing: blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared raw, so a different-case variant of a blocked address bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS (confidence=95, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 + handler.ts:74-83 — no cap on guest array size and no in-request dedup; a caller can submit hundreds/thousands of emails in one call, each triggering a separate transactional email — an email-bombing/mail-relay-abuse primitive with no visible rate limiting (confidence=85, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-49 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` (AND instead of OR) fails closed, denying legitimate non-owner team admins rather than granting excess access (confidence=60, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager constructed with the calling user's own credentials (not the organizer's) then used to mutate the organizer's calendar event, a credential-scoping mistake when an attendee (not organizer) invokes the mutation (confidence=55, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-165 — attendee rows are committed via createMany before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, with no transaction/rollback; if calendar sync fails the guest rows are already persisted and undoable only via manual DB intervention since retries are rejected by the dedup check as "already present" (confidence=90, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-90 + addGuests.schema.ts:1-7 — duplicate emails within the same request array are never deduped and Attendee has no @@unique(bookingId,email) constraint, so createMany will happily insert multiple identical-email attendee rows for one booking (confidence=85, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email send failures swallowed after DB write and calendar sync already succeeded; attendees end up added with no notification and no retry/error-tracking path (confidence=80, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:88 — `locale: organizer.locale` is written explicitly, so a null organizer locale writes null into Attendee.locale instead of letting Prisma apply its "en" default; currently harmless due to downstream `?? "en"` guards but a silent divergence from schema intent (confidence=70, P3).
